findings: SCHEMA AMENDMENT FILED AND APPLIED (AMENDMENT-W1-10-01, six defects, all the same root cause: moveset.schema.json was never rebased under seam S22 and its enums were transcribed from prose rather than from the tables). active_f max 16 forbade five classes' published jump.r1; recovery_f max 90 forbade GHM/UGS jump.r1; startup_f max 90 forbade GHM/UGS R2; charge_max_f max 60 forbade bow.aimed's published 90; trigger.button carried 8 of HARNESS.md §4's 14 names and omitted swap_left, which RI-WPN06 §C's mandatory O2 slots require; slotId omitted r1.5 which RI-WPN01 §A slot 4 points at and FST's 5-chain needs; hitstop_f omitted `wood` which RI-WPN05 §A's grid publishes; slots.minProperties 25 denied BOW the reduced 7-slot table RI-WPN01 §A grants it in prose. 3/87 files validated before, 87/87 after.

SHARE(c) <= 4 (RI-WPN03 §C) FORCES ARI >= 0.318 for this census. A class of 8 cannot have one shared moveset, so the minimum distinct-clip count any conforming roster can have is sum over classes of 25*ceil(N/4) = 664. The ARI >= 0.26 pass bar sits BELOW the floor its own item's SHARE cap imposes, and the ARI < 0.19 hard-fail bar is unreachable by any conforming roster. Offered as bar_pressure evidence.

Dg_min IS SUBSTANTIALLY A MEASUREMENT OF RI-WPN02 §B, NOT OF THE BUILD. Four of Dg's five grammar dimensions (chain length, arc, root displacement, recovery ratio) are fully determined by §B's published table; only D11 (hyperarmour fraction) is a build decision, and it is one scalar being asked to separate fifteen classes at once. §B alone puts AXE and HLB 0.49 apart before a builder writes anything. Proposed remedy: add a sixth grammar dimension for MATERIAL RESPONSE (multiplier spread across materials + deflection bypass) — RI-WPN02 §C uses exactly that property to define the mace, and the fingerprint that decides whether the mace is a real class cannot see it.

RI-WPN02 §B's OWN UGS ROW VIOLATES RI-WPN02 M5: shape slash_v at arc 210 deg with root 1.40 m, while M5 says slash_v implies arc < 130 and root < 0.7. Implemented §B verbatim for the UGS baseline (the table wins over the check on it) and reported rather than repaired.

RI-WPN06 §B's chain-length-change examples are unimplementable in the direction stated: r1.3 AND 2h.r1.3 are both in RI-WPN01 §A's mandatory 25, so neither chain can be shorter than 3 without a mandatory slot becoming unreachable. Four classes change grip length UPWARD through the optional fourth link instead (DGR 4->3, CSW 4->3, TSW 3->4, CGS 3->4), which meets the >=4 requirement.

RI-WPN05 §E's peak-tip-speed bands and RI-WPN02 §B's (arc, active frames, reach) are not mutually satisfiable for WHP: 200 deg over a 10-frame active window at 3.60 m gives 62 m/s at a CONSTANT swing rate against a medium band of 18-26. 7/15 classes in band; anticipation 15/15; follow-through 14/15. RI-WPN05 is W1-11's item by PLAN.md §3.

RI-WPN05 §F's ILS cannot reach 1.00 from §A/§C as published: flesh and wood have identical hitstop in every tier and identical knockback, so no classifier can separate them. Ceiling from the table alone is 0.771; the deflection rule is what lifts the measured value to 0.80.

A SIGNATURE WEAPON MUST LIVE IN A LINEAGE OF >= 3. In a 2-member lineage, one member's override makes the OTHER member's inherited clip used by exactly one weapon, so it counts toward that weapon's UNQ and turns it into a signature too — RI-WPN03 M5 caps a class at two. Real property of the UNQ definition; the fix is the roster's shape.

OUR OWN TOOL FOUND A REAL FORGERY: five classes had run.r1 and run.r2 on the same pose family with the same frame derivation, producing 16 pairs of byte-identical clips under different ids. run.r2 now derives from the class R2 row with its own pose family (run_leap). Forged pairs 16 -> 0 of 641,278.

The generator must NOT read its own previous output. An earlier version fed measured fingerprint standard deviations back into the deviation budget; it had a 2-cycle and six weapon files alternated forever, so `--check` reported drift on every run. The sds are now pinned in classes.json and fp-sd.json is written as a report only.
ar3_seam: The material system. A lore fact (root-golems are stone, the Hist-bonded are plant) is a combat answer: a slashing weapon does x0.45 to stone and DEFLECTS off it (zero damage, +16 f@60 recovery, spark decal), a smash weapon does x1.35 and never bounces, and MCE/GHM bypass deflection entirely. Inside the fight it is Souls-legal (geometry decides the hit, the multiplier is applied after, no dice); outside it, learning which material a thing is made of is a rumour or a book, and the answer is a purchase from a merchant. seam_sterile: false.

notes_for_successor: Regenerate, never hand-edit the 87 files: `node tools/weapons/build-movesets.mjs` (idempotent; `--check` must report zero drift). The three authored sources are classes.json (transcribed corpus tables, do not re-derive), pose-library.json (the pose grammar) and roster.json (direction and rank of each weapon's deviation; the generator sets magnitude). tools/weapons/measure.mjs recomputes all seven headline numbers from the shipped data plus the real rig and is the file to diff against if a critic gets different numbers. The three knobs that move the fingerprint results are classes.json deviation_budget / deviation_budget_signature / lineage_arc_scale and the per-class ha_extra ladder in tools/weapons/grammar.mjs; changing any of them requires re-running the measure to check SEP and W_med are still in band.
